At Phillip Riley we are looking for an experienced Geotechnical Engineer to join our team.

As the Geotechnical Engineer you will be responsible for dealing with the mechanics of soil and rock and its applications to engineering elements.

Main tasks will include:

You will deal with the analysis, design and construction of man-made structures or systems that are made of or are supported by soil or rock.
Identify, design and implement practical solutions to engineering problems concerning soil, rock and groundwater.
Apply scientific and engineering techniques to predict and manage the behaviour of the ground where it interacts with or responds to human activity.
Plan, direct and conduct survey work to analyse the likely behaviour of soil and rock when placed under pressure by proposed structures, and designs above and below ground foundations.
Obtaining soil and rock samples at different depths across sites and testing samples to determine strength, compressibility and other factors that affect the behaviour of soil and rock when a structure is imposed and determining the safe loading for the soil
Plans, directs and conducts survey work to analyse the likely behaviour of soil and rock when placed under pressure by proposed structures, and designs above and below ground foundations
Key skills:

Problem solving
Communication
Project management
Teamwork
Analytical abilities
Soil mechanics
Adaptability
Analysis
Data collection
Research
Slope stability
Environmental and geographical factors
Geotechnical analysis
Ability to apply technical knowledge
Ensure compliance with all regulatory standards
Geotechnical design
Minimum of 1 year experience required

Lead Safety. Build Culture. Make a Real Difference.

Are you a passionate safety professional who knows that great safety outcomes are built on trust, influence and genuine engagement with people?

We are seeking an experienced Safety Manager to join a diverse and growing organisation based in Wangaratta, supporting a workforce of approximately 300 employees across multiple operational environments including manufacturing, warehousing and field-based technical services.

This is an opportunity to step into a highly visible leadership role where you will shape safety strategy, influence business performance and help create a workplace where everyone goes home safe every day.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will lead and drive the Health, Safety and Wellbeing function across multiple sites and operational activities. You will develop, implement and continuously improve safety systems, ensuring compliance while fostering a practical, positive and people-focused safety culture.

You will be responsible for:

* Developing, implementing and managing the organisation's OHS Operational Plan
* Acting as the organisation's Return to Work (RTW) Coordinator
* Leading risk management activities, including hazard identification, risk assessments and controls
* Delivering and coordinating safety training, coaching and capability development
* Supporting managers and employees with task design, reasonable adjustments and injury prevention initiatives
* Facilitating meaningful consultation with employees, Health and Safety Representatives and key stakeholders
* Leading incident investigations using recognised methodologies such as ICAM, Root Cause Analysis and other contemporary investigation techniques
* Ensuring corrective actions are practical, effective and embedded into business operations
* Maintaining compliance with legislative, regulatory and reporting requirements
* Managing safety records, reporting systems and digital safety management tools
* Developing safety metrics, reporting insights and recommendations to support business decision-making
* Driving continuous improvement across all safety and wellbeing programs

About You

You are more than a compliance professional, you are a genuine leader who can connect with people, earn trust and positively influence behaviours at every level of an organisation.

You will bring:

Essential Requirements

* Minimum Certificate IV in Work Health & Safety or Occupational Health & Safety
* Demonstrated experience in a similar Safety Manager, Safety Advisor or Health & Safety leadership role within manufacturing, industrial, logistics, warehousing, technical services or a comparable operational environment
* Experience as a Return to Work Coordinator
* Strong capability in risk management, safety systems and operational safety leadership
* Proven experience leading complex incident investigations and implementing sustainable corrective actions
* Excellent knowledge of reporting procedures, record-keeping requirements and safety management systems
* Strong understanding and application of digital reporting and safety management platforms

Comprehensive knowledge of:
* Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Victoria)
* Victorian OHS Regulations
* Relevant Australian Standards and industry best practice
* Current driver's licence

Personal Attributes
We are looking for someone who:

* Leads with authenticity, integrity and accountability
* Has an open, approachable and engaging communication style
* Can confidently influence and coach leaders, supervisors and frontline employees
* Builds strong relationships across all levels of the organisation and with external stakeholders
* Balances commercial understanding with a genuine commitment to safety and legal compliance
* Is highly organised, proactive and solutions-focused
* Thrives in a hands-on environment and enjoys being visible in the workplace rather than behind a desk

Why Join Us?

* Attractive $100K++ salary and benefits package
* Key leadership position with genuine influence across the organisation
* Diverse operational environment providing variety and challenge
* Opportunity to shape safety culture and drive meaningful change
* Work with a business that values people, safety and continuous improvement
* Enjoy the lifestyle benefits of living and working in beautiful regional Wangaratta

Ready to Lead the Way?

If you're a people-first safety professional with the experience, credibility and passion to create safer workplaces and stronger safety cultures, we'd love to hear from you.

Contact Dan Sawyer for a PD and more information in confidence on 0403 899143

Worrells is a fast growing, specialist accounting firm with expertise in solvency management and insolvency administration. We have carved a successful niche in the small to medium enterprise market by delivering quality service and processes with our unique systems. Established in 1973, Worrells now have 36 principals in 28 locations across NSW, QLD, ACT, VIC and WA, we draw upon broader resources and technical expertise enabling us to be focused locally while being resourced nationally.

We are looking for a full time Insolvency Accountant to join our NSW/ACT team based in Parramatta NSW. The successful candidate will be responsible for:

Day to day file management of insolvency appointments (from start to finish)
Preparation of statutory lodgements
Liaising with directors, employees, creditors, banks, statutory authorities and other stakeholders
Collection and investigation into records
Prioritise and manage workloads to meet conflicting deadlines
Analyse financial statements and diverse financial data
Drafting of reports and preparation of creditors meetings
Investigations into insolvent trading, voidable transactions and offences committed by officers
Attending sites to inspect, collect and record assets and books and records
Assisting with Fair Entitlements Guarantee claims and calculating employee entitlements.

We are seeking a candidate who has:

Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office (Words, Excel, Outlook)
A Bachelor Degree or equivalent in Commerce, Finance or Accounting
Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal)
CA or CPA qualified (or willing to obtain)
ARITA Introduction to Insolvency certification
ARITA professional qualification (or willing to obtain)
Previous experience in insolvency is required.

We understand the importance of work-life balance, and we offer flexibility to support your needs. You'll become part of a collaborative team of professionals who are dedicated to both their work and personal growth. We provide opportunities for ongoing learning and development, and you'll have access to resources that will help you advance in your career. Worrells is committed to your professional growth, and we'll provide the support you need to succeed.

Location: Arundel, QLD, 4214
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Workshop Foreman / Production Manager
Job Title: Cabinet Maker
Salary range: $79,500 - $86,600 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role:
We are seeking a highly skilled and detail-oriented Cabinetmaker for a full-time, permanent position within our client's advanced workshop. This role is central to the production of custom-made cabinets, fine furniture, and specialized commercial fit outs. The successful candidate will be responsible for interpreting complex designs and transforming premium materials into finished articles of outstanding quality, from initial fabrication through to final finishing and hardware installation.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Project Analysis & Specification Planning:
• Meticulously examine and interpret detailed workshop drawings, CAD designs, work orders, and sample components to determine precise construction specifications and methodologies.
• Select and prepare premium materials including solid timber, veneers, particle board, and specialized engineered wood products appropriate for each project's functional and aesthetic requirements.

Precision Manufacturing & Machining:
• Program, set up, and operate Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machinery to accurately mark out, cut, shape, and profile components with exceptional efficiency and accuracy.
• Fabricate bespoke cabinets, freestanding furniture, and specialized fittings—including those for marine and automotive interiors—utilizing both advanced machinery and traditional hand-tool techniques to achieve fine detail.

Expert Assembly & Finishing:
• Assemble prepared components and sub-assemblies to form complete sections and finished articles, ensuring perfect alignment, structural integrity, and seamless construction.
• Skilfully apply protective and decorative finishes through sanding, staining, sealing, and coating processes to achieve a superior, client-specified surface quality on all cabinetry and furniture.

Hardware Fitting & Installation Support:
• Precisely fit and calibrate all associated hardware including hinges, locks, catches, drawer runners, and shelving systems to ensure flawless operation and longevity.
• Participate in the on-site installation and final fitting of cabinetry for kitchens, bathrooms, and commercial fit-outs, conducting necessary adjustments to ensure a perfect finish.

Specialist Fabrication & Restoration:
• Construct frames and build custom fittings for upholstered items such as chairs and couches, adhering to specific design and durability requirements.
• Potentially engage in the careful reproduction of period furniture or the expert repair and refurbishment of antique and contemporary pieces, utilizing appropriate restorative techniques.

Skills & Experience Required:
Essential Qualifications & Experience:
• A formal qualification such as a Certificate III in Cabinet Making or equivalent is essential.
• Proven post-apprenticeship experience (minimum 2+ years) within a high-end cabinetmaking, furniture manufacturing, or specialist joinery workshop environment.
• Demonstrable experience working with a broad range of materials including solid timber, veneers, and engineered boards.

Technical Proficiencies:
• High competency in programming, operating, and maintaining CNC machinery and CAD software for component production.
• Advanced skills in traditional cabinetmaking joinery, precision assembly, and hand-finishing techniques.
• Proven ability to install cabinetry and fittings on-site with a focus on precise integration.

Personal Attributes:
• An artisan's eye for detail and a steadfast commitment to producing work of the highest craftsmanship and quality.
• A methodical, problem-solving approach with the ability to work independently and manage workflow to meet deadlines.
• Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset to work effectively with workshop colleagues and design staff.
• The physical capability to handle workshop duties, including lifting materials and standing for extended periods.

What’s On Offer:
This role offers a skilled tradesperson the opportunity to work on prestigious, varied projects with premium materials in a supportive, well-resourced environment. The position comes with a permanent full-time contract and a competitive salary package reflective of experience and skill level.

Application Process:
If you possess the craftsmanship and technical skills required for this specialist cabinetmaking role, please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.
We are acting as an exclusive recruitment agent for this position. Our client's identity is protected under our agency agreement.
